q: Sharding 的核心定义是什么？
q_en: What is the core definition of sharding?
options: 把一个表拆成多个逻辑分区，但仍放在同一台数据库机器上
把数据水平拆分到多台独立数据库机器上，每个 shard 持有一部分数据
只把冷数据迁移到对象存储
给单个数据库实例加更多 CPU 和内存
options_en: Split one table into logical partitions but keep it on the same database machine.
Horizontally split data across multiple independent database machines, where each shard holds part of the data.
Just move cold data off to object storage.
Add more CPU and memory to a single database instance.
why: Sharding 在系统设计里通常指数据层/数据库/存储的水平分片：同一张逻辑表按 shard key 分到多台 DB 节点。服务层也会横向扩容，但通常叫 replicas/load balancing，不叫数据库 sharding。
why_en: In system-design interviews, sharding usually means horizontally splitting data across database or storage nodes. Service instances can also scale horizontally, but that is usually called replicas or load balancing, not database sharding.
optionExplanations: 把数据放在单机而不是多台机器上，这是 partitioning 的定义而非 sharding。
这正是 sharding 的核心定义，把数据跨多台机器分散。
这是数据归档而不是分片，不涉及跨机器分布。
这只是垂直扩展，无法扩展到多台机器的吞吐和存储。
optionExplanations_en: Putting data on one machine in partitions is partitioning, not sharding.
This is the core definition of sharding: distributing data across multiple independent machines.
Cold data archival is data management, not distribution across machines.
Vertical scaling with more CPU or memory cannot distribute throughput and storage.

Partitioning 通常是在单个数据库实例内拆数据；Sharding 是把数据拆到多台机器
Partitioning 只能拆列，Sharding 只能拆索引
两者没有任何语义差异，永远完全等价
options_en: Partitioning always spans machines and sharding always stays inside one machine.
Partitioning usually splits data inside a single database instance; sharding splits data across multiple machines.
Partitioning can only split columns and sharding can only split indexes.
The two terms have no semantic difference and are always exactly equivalent.
why: 工程实践里两词常被混用，但技术上 partitioning 更常指单实例内分区，sharding 强调跨机器分布。面试里要说明数据到底在一台机器还是多台机器。
why_en: Partitioning usually means splitting data inside one database instance, while sharding means splitting it across multiple machines.
tradeoff: partitioning（单机内组织数据，不加机器）vs sharding（跨机器分布数据，换来更多容量和吞吐）

判断标准很简单：只要数据跨过不止一台服务器，就该叫 sharding。
拆列和拆索引是两回事，单机切分既能按行也能按列。
口语上常混用，但面试官仍期待你说清楚数据落在几台机器上。

Simple test: if the data spans more than one server, call it sharding.
Splitting columns and splitting indexes are different things; single-machine splitting can go either way.
The words get used loosely in practice, but interviewers still expect you to name how many machines the data spans.

q: 关于单机内 partitioning，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about single-machine partitioning are correct? (Select all that apply.)
options: Horizontal partitioning 按行拆，例如按年份拆 orders
Vertical partitioning 按列拆，例如把大字段或冷字段拆到另一张表
Partitioning 本身不会增加数据库机器数量
Partitioning 一定能把写吞吐扩展到多台机器
options_en: Horizontal partitioning splits rows, for example partitioning orders by year.
Vertical partitioning splits columns, for example moving large or cold columns into another table.
Partitioning by itself does not add more database machines.
Partitioning always scales write throughput across multiple machines.
why: 单机内 partitioning 的关键词是「同一台数据库实例」。Horizontal 按行拆，vertical 按列拆；它能减少扫描和维护范围，但不会把写吞吐扩展到多台机器。
why_en: Single-machine partitioning stays inside one database instance. Horizontal partitioning splits rows and vertical partitioning splits columns; it can reduce scan and maintenance scope, but it does not add machines or scale writes across machines.
whenOtherWins: 同一字段可以参与多层 key，但职责不同；高写入系统不要把单调递增的 created_at 同时当 shard key 和 partition key。
codeSample:
# 三个 key 可以不同，各管一层
# shard key: 选哪台数据库机器
# partition key: 选这台机器里的哪个粗粒度分区
# sort/index key: 在分区内快速定位和排序

def route_order(order):
    shard_id = hash(order.user_id) % NUM_SHARDS       # DB machine
    partition = month(order.created_at)               # orders_2026_06
    index_key = (order.user_id, -order.created_at)     # newest first
    insert(shard_id, f"orders_{partition}", order, index_key)

# partition 只把 10 年数据缩小到 1 个月；这个月里仍可能有千万行
# index/sort key 再在 6 月分区内快速找到 user 42，并按 created_at 倒序读
query(user_id=42, month="2026-06", order_by="created_at DESC")
optionExplanations: 正确，水平分片就是按行分组，按条件（如年份）拆表。
正确，垂直分片就是把不同列拆到不同表或存储。
正确，单实例 partitioning 只改善数据组织，不增加机器数。
错误，单机分区不能把写吞吐扩展到多机器，那需要 sharding。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; horizontal partitioning splits rows by condition, for example by year.
Correct; vertical partitioning splits columns into separate tables or storage.
Correct; partitioning within one instance does not add database machines.
Incorrect; partitioning alone cannot scale write throughput to multiple machines; that requires sharding.

q: 这个阶段优先考虑什么？

options: 跳过分区，直接引入 64 个 shard 做水平扩展
先在单机内按时间做 partitioning，让查询只扫相关分区
删掉表上的所有索引来提升扫描速度
把全部历史订单迁移进 Redis 当主存储
options_en: Skip partitioning and jump straight to 64 shards for horizontal scaling.
First partition by time inside the single instance so queries only scan the relevant slice.
Delete every index on the table to speed up scans.
Move all historical orders into Redis as the primary store.
why: 如果瓶颈是大表扫描、索引/维护范围或历史数据清理，单机 partitioning 可能足够。它不会加机器，但能让数据库少扫、少维护、好清理。

q: 一个好的 shard key 通常需要满足哪些性质？（多选）
q_en: What properties does a good shard key usually need? (Select all that apply.)
options: 高基数，有很多不同取值
数据和流量分布尽量均匀
和主要查询模式对齐，使常见查询命中单个 shard
值越少越好，最好只有 true/false
options_en: High cardinality, with many distinct values
Data and traffic distribute evenly across shards
It matches primary query patterns, so common queries hit a single shard
The fewer values the better — ideally just true and false

why_en: A good shard key has high cardinality, balanced distribution, and matches the dominant query patterns.
optionExplanations: 正确，高基数意味着 key 有很多可能值，能打散数据。
正确，均匀分布能避免热点 shard 和数据倾斜。
正确，贴合查询模式的 shard key 能减少跨 shard 操作。
错误，基数太低反而会导致严重倾斜和热点。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; high cardinality means many distinct values, distributing data better.
Correct; balanced traffic distribution avoids hotspot shards and data skew.
Correct; a shard key aligned with query patterns reduces cross-shard operations.
Incorrect; low cardinality keys cause severe imbalance and hot spots.

只有两个取值，最多天然分成两个大组，且很容易严重倾斜
boolean 会让所有查询变成跨 shard
boolean 字段无法建立索引

It only has two values, so at most it splits into two groups, and one easily ends up far larger than the other.
A boolean shard key forces every query to become cross-shard.

why_en: A boolean shard key has extremely low cardinality and tends to create only two imbalanced shards.

不准确，boolean shard key 会导致倾斜和热点，但不一定所有查询都跨 shard。
错误，boolean 字段完全可以建立索引。

Correct; a boolean has only two values, creating at most two imbalanced groups.
Not quite; a boolean key causes skew and imbalance, but not all queries necessarily fan out.
Incorrect; boolean fields can be indexed like any other column.

美国 shard 变热点，其他相对空闲
查询会自动变成 O(1)

The US shard becomes a hotspot while the others sit relatively idle.

对：90% 用户集中在美国，等于把绝大部分数据和请求压到一个 shard 上。

错：分片内部仍然需要索引来加速本地查询。

q: 按 `created_at` 对持续增长的写入表做 range sharding，最常见的问题是什么？
q_en: What is the common problem with range sharding a constantly growing write table by `created_at`?
options: 所有新写入都打到最新时间范围的 shard，形成写热点
所有历史 shard 都会被均匀写入
短时间内不能查询最近数据
时间字段不能用于排序
options_en: All new writes land on the shard for the newest time range, creating a write hotspot.
All historical shards get written to evenly.
You can't query recent data for a while.
Time fields can no longer be used for sorting.
why: 你的理解对：持续写入表里的 `created_at` 基本都是 now，所以 range router 会把新写入都送到最新时间范围的 shard。旧 shard 主要读历史，新 shard 扛全部写入，热点就出现了。
why_en: Because new rows have created_at close to now, a range router sends almost all inserts to the newest time-range shard. Older shards mostly serve historical reads, while the newest shard carries the write load.
whenOtherWins: 按时间 range sharding 适合历史归档、按时间范围扫描、冷数据分层；高写入主链路更常用 hash(user_id/order_id/tenant_id) 打散，或用 time bucket + hash 子分片。

Shard A: created_at < 2026-07-01
Shard B: 2026-07-01 <= created_at < 2026-07-08
Shard C: created_at >= 2026-07-08

错误，历史 shard 往往只接收读流量，新 shard 会被写入压垮。
错误，可以立即查询最近数据，他们就在最新 shard 上。
错误，时间字段本身仍可用于排序。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; time-range sharding concentrates all new writes in the newest time-range shard.
Incorrect; older shards receive mostly reads while the newest shard is overwhelmed with writes.
Incorrect; you can query recent data immediately; it lives in the newest shard.
Incorrect; time fields can still be used for sorting just fine.

q: Range-based sharding 是怎么分配数据的？
q_en: How does range-based sharding assign data?
options: 对 shard key 取 hash 后再取模决定 shard
按连续的 key 值区间分配到不同 shard
先查目录服务，得到映射后才路由到 shard
每次写入随机挑一个 shard
options_en: Hash the shard key and take it modulo the shard count.
Assign continuous ranges of the key's values to different shards.
Look up a directory service to get the mapping before routing.
Pick a random shard for every write.
why: Range sharding 把连续 key 区间分给不同 shard，简单且保留范围查询能力；代价是访问模式一旦倾斜，流量会挤在少数 shard。
why_en: Range-based sharding assigns continuous key ranges to shards, which is simple and supports range scans.
codeSample:
Shard 1 -> user_id 1        - 1,000,000
Shard 2 -> user_id 1,000,001 - 2,000,000
Shard 3 -> user_id 2,000,001 - 3,000,000
# a range query like id 500K-600K only touches Shard 1
optionExplanations: 错，先 hash 再取模是 hash sharding 的做法。
对：这题描述的正是把连续区间分配给 shard 的做法。
错，先查目录服务才能定位数据是 directory sharding。
错，随机写入会让你彻底找不到数据在哪个 shard。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; hash-then-modulo is how hash sharding routes.
Correct; this describes assigning continuous ranges to shards.
Incorrect; looking up a directory first is the directory-based sharding approach.
Incorrect; random writes make it impossible to know which shard holds a given row.

q: Hash-based sharding 的基本路由方式是什么？
q_en: What is the basic routing rule for hash-based sharding?
options: shard key 取 hash 取模选 shard
按当前日期所在月份决定 shard
由用户手动指定 shard
数据库每次随机选一个 shard
options_en: Hash the shard key, then take it modulo the shard count.
Decide the shard from the current calendar month.
Let the user manually specify the shard.
Have the database pick a random shard every time.
why: Hash sharding 把 key 打散到 hash 空间，再映射到 shard。常见表达是 `hash(user_id) % N`。
why_en: Hash sharding hashes the shard key and maps the hash result to a shard, often using modulo.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Request key"] --> B["hash key"]
  B --> C["route to shard"]
  C --> D["read or write row"]
codeSample:
shard = hash(user_id) % 4

User 42  -> hash(42)  % 4 = 2   # Shard 2
User 99  -> hash(99)  % 4 = 3   # Shard 3
User 123 -> hash(123) % 4 = 1   # Shard 1
optionExplanations: 对：这是 hash sharding 的标准路由公式。
错，这是时间范围分片，不是 hash 分片。
错，手动选择不可靠且不可扩展。
错，随机决定会导致数据定位困难且增加路由开销。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; this is hash-based sharding's standard routing formula.
Incorrect; that is time-range sharding, not hash sharding.
Incorrect; manual selection is unreliable and does not scale.
Incorrect; random routing makes data location unpredictable and routing expensive.

q: 简单 `hash(key) % N` 在从 4 个 shard 扩到 5 个 shard 时有什么问题？
q_en: What goes wrong with simple `hash(key) % N` when scaling from 4 shards to 5?
options: 几乎所有 key 的映射都可能改变，需要迁移大量数据
所有 key 都继续留在原 shard
只能新增空 shard，永远不迁移
会自动保证只迁移 1/N 数据
options_en: Almost every key's mapping can change, requiring large-scale data migration.
All keys stay on their original shard.
You can only add empty shards and never migrate anything.
It automatically guarantees only 1/N of the data moves.
why: N 改变会改变取模结果，大量 key 会重新映射到新 shard。扩容前必须有 resharding 计划。
why_en: Modulo-based hashing remaps many keys when the shard count changes, causing massive data movement.
optionExplanations: 正确，N 从 4 变到 5 后，取模结果改变，大量 key 会重新映射。
错误，取模改变后 key 的目标 shard 会改变，需要迁移。
错误，无法只新增 shard，之前数据仍需要重映射。
错误，简单模运算不能自动控制迁移量，一致性哈希才能做到。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; changing N from four to five alters the modulo result for most keys.
Incorrect; keys remapped to different shards require data migration.
Incorrect; you cannot just add new empty shards without remapping existing data.
Incorrect; simple modulo hashing does not automatically limit migration volume; consistent hashing does.

scenario: 你用 hash sharding，但希望新增或移除 shard 时只迁移一小部分数据。

q: 应该引入什么思想？
q_en: What idea should you introduce?
options: Consistent hashing
Boolean shard key
全表扫描
只写单库
options_en: Consistent hashing
A boolean shard key
A full table scan
Write to a single database only
why: 公式不是 `hash(key) % N`，而是 `h = H(key)` 后在 hash ring 上找顺时针第一个节点。新增节点只接走它前一个节点到自己之间的 key 范围。
why_en: The rule is not hash(key) % N. Compute h=H(key), then choose the first node clockwise on the hash ring. A new node only takes the key range between its predecessor and itself.
whenOtherWins: 节点集合固定且很小时，简单 modulo 更容易；节点会频繁增减时，一致性哈希更稳。
tradeoff: consistent hashing（扩缩容迁移少）vs modulo（实现简单但改 N 后大量重映射）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  K["H(key)=42"] --> A["clockwise"]
  A --> B["first node >= 42"]
  B --> C["Shard B"]
optionExplanations: 对：环上只有相邻的一小段 key 会被重新分配，其余留在原地，这是它比简单取模稳的原因。
错，boolean shard key 基数太低，和扩容迁移量无关。
错，全表扫描是查询方式，不解决节点增减时的迁移问题。
错，单库没法扩容，也就没有'加节点减少迁移'这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; only a small neighboring slice of the ring gets reassigned, which is why it's steadier than plain modulo.
Incorrect; a boolean shard key's low cardinality is unrelated to migration volume during resizing.
Incorrect; a full table scan is a query pattern, not a fix for node-change migration.
Incorrect; a single database can't be resized, so there's no 'add a node, migrate less' problem to solve.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps nodes and keys onto the same hash ring, so adding or removing a node only remaps a small neighboring range.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一台物理节点放到 hash ring 的多个位置，让数据分布更均匀。

q: Directory-based sharding 的核心机制是什么？
q_en: What is the core mechanism of directory-based sharding?
options: 用固定公式（如 hash 取模）直接算出 shard
查一张映射表，记录每个 key 当前在哪个 shard
只能按时间范围切分，没有其他方式
完全不需要任何路由层来定位数据
options_en: Compute the shard directly with a fixed formula such as hash-and-modulo.
Look up a mapping table that records which shard each key currently lives on.
It can only split data by time ranges.
It needs no routing layer at all to locate data.
why: Directory sharding 不用公式，而是查一张映射表来定位某个 key 当前在哪个 shard；最大优点是灵活，可以单独搬迁任意一条记录。
why_en: Directory-based sharding uses a lookup table or service to map each key to its shard.

flowchart LR
  A["Client"] --> B["Directory map"]
  B --> C["Shard A"]
  B --> D["Shard B"]
  B --> E["Shard C"]

user_to_shard
-------------
15  -> shard-1
87  -> shard-4
204 -> shard-2
# every request queries this table before routing

对：先查映射表，再决定去哪个 shard，这就是 directory 的核心机制。
错，只按值区间切分是 range sharding 的特征；directory 用的是显式映射。
错，directory 恰恰需要一层路由/查找服务，否则没人知道数据在哪。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; routing by a fixed formula is how hash or range sharding works, not directory sharding.
Correct; looking up the mapping table first, then routing, is directory sharding's core mechanism.
Incorrect; splitting only by value ranges is range sharding's trait; directory sharding uses an explicit map.
Incorrect; directory sharding specifically needs a routing or lookup layer, or nobody knows where data lives.

q: Directory-based sharding 相比 hash/range 的典型取舍是什么？（多选）
q_en: What are the typical tradeoffs of directory-based sharding compared with hash or range sharding? (Select all that apply.)
options: 更灵活，可以单独迁移热用户或复杂分配
每次请求多一次目录查找，增加延迟
目录服务变成关键依赖，故障会影响全系统路由

options_en: More flexible — it can migrate a single hot user or apply complex assignment logic.
Every request adds one extra directory lookup, increasing latency.
The directory service becomes a critical dependency; its failure breaks routing system-wide.

why: Directory 的灵活性来自显式映射：可以把 user 42 单独指到 shard-9。但请求路径多了一步查目录；目录服务慢或挂了，即使数据 shard 正常也不知道该去哪。
why_en: Directory sharding is flexible because explicit mappings can route user 42 to shard-9. But the request path adds a directory lookup; if the directory is slow or down, healthy data shards still cannot be reached.

query(shard, user_id)

shard = directory.get(user_id)   # extra lookup: Redis/DB/config service
query(shard, user_id)

错误，目录服务故障或高延迟会直接影响系统可用性。

options: 数据库缓存命中率很高
所有 shard 都完全均衡
某 shard 数据/流量远超其他，成为瓶颈
某个 shard 的数据永远不被访问
options_en: The database's cache hit rate is very high.
All shards are perfectly balanced.
One shard's data or traffic far exceeds the others and becomes the bottleneck.
One shard's data is never accessed.

q: 最好的事务设计方向是什么？
q_en: What is the best direction for transaction design?

故意把每个字段放到不同 shard
所有操作都用 2PC
同用户数据聚合到一个 shard

Deliberately spread every field across different shards.
Use two-phase commit for every operation.
Aggregate one user's data onto a single shard.

why_en: The best design keeps related user data on one shard so normal single-shard transactions still work.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务天然跨用户或跨 tenant，例如转账，就需要 saga、异步补偿或接受更复杂的一致性方案。

optionExplanations: 错误，缓存不能替代数据库作为持久化。
错误，分散数据会导致强制需要跨 shard 事务。
错误，不是所有操作都需要 2PC，只有必要时才用。
正确，把用户相关数据聚合在同一 shard，可以用普通单库事务。

Incorrect; scattering data forces unnecessary cross-shard transactions.

从 User A 所在 shard 扣钱

补偿动作把 User A 的扣款退回

why_en: A saga coordinates cross-shard work through independent steps plus compensating actions on failure.

flowchart TD

scenario_en: A user's `follower_count` is denormalized across several shards to speed up profile reads, so counts may disagree briefly across shards.
q: 这类场景通常可以接受什么一致性模型？
q_en: What consistency model is usually acceptable for this kind of scenario?
options: 所有读都锁住全站
每次读都必须 2PC
禁止缓存和反范式化
最终一致，异步收敛
options_en: Lock the entire site for every read
Every read must go through two-phase commit
Ban caching and denormalization entirely
Eventually consistent, converging asynchronously
why: 计数类展示通常允许几秒延迟，最终收敛即可。为了这类低风险数据强行做分布式事务，复杂度不值得。
why_en: Denormalized counters often tolerate eventual consistency because brief inconsistencies are acceptable.
whenOtherWins: 库存扣减、资金转账这类强正确性场景不能轻易接受短暂错误，需要更强事务或补偿设计。
tradeoff: eventual consistency（快、简单，短暂不一致）vs 强一致/2PC（每次读写都准确，但要跨 shard 协调，慢且脆弱）
optionExplanations: 错：全站锁会把所有并发读写都串行化，代价极大。
错：给每次读加 2PC，性能代价远超这类展示型数据值得的程度。
错：反范式化和缓存正是为了减少昂贵的跨 shard 查询，不该禁止。
对：几秒内不同 shard 数字略有出入没关系，后台任务最终会把它们收敛成同一个值。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; a site-wide lock serializes all concurrent reads and writes at a huge cost.
Incorrect; adding two-phase commit to every read costs far more than this display-only data is worth.
Incorrect; denormalization and caching exist precisely to cut expensive cross-shard queries, not to be banned.
Correct; a few seconds of disagreement between shards is fine, since a background job eventually converges them.

q_en: How do modern databases usually help you handle sharding? (Select all that apply.)
options: 让你指定 partition key 或 shard key
自动处理路由、分裂/迁移或再平衡中的一部分
完全消除 shard key 选择带来的所有后果
在不同产品中使用完全相同的内部机制
options_en: Let you specify a partition key or shard key
Automatically handle part of the routing, splitting/migration, or rebalancing
Completely eliminate every consequence of your shard key choice
Use exactly the same internal mechanism across different products
why: Cassandra、DynamoDB、MongoDB、Vitess/Citus 等会帮你处理很多路由和再平衡细节，但 shard key 选择仍会决定热点和查询形状。

optionExplanations: 正确，现代数据库通常要求你指定 partition/shard key。
正确，现代数据库自动处理很多分片细节，减少手动工作。
错误，即使自动处理，shard key 选择仍会影响热点和查询形状。
错误，不同数据库用不同内部机制，虽然对用户来说大致相似。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; modern databases let you specify a partition or shard key.
Correct; they automate routing, splitting, migration, and rebalancing work.
Incorrect; automation does not eliminate the impact of shard key choice.

scenario: 面试官追问 Cassandra、DynamoDB、MongoDB 这三款常见 NoSQL 数据库，是不是都靠同一套一致性哈希在背后自动分片。
scenario_en: An interviewer asks whether Cassandra, DynamoDB, and MongoDB all use the exact same consistent-hashing mechanism for automatic sharding.
q: 关于它们的 sharding 机制，哪种说法更准确？
q_en: Which statement about their sharding mechanisms is more accurate?
options: 它们都用完全相同的 classic ring 一致性哈希实现
它们都按 key 分布数据，但内部分片机制并不相同
它们都只能手工路由查询，没有自动分片
它们都不支持后续扩容
options_en: They all use exactly the same classic-ring consistent hashing implementation.
They all distribute data by key, but their internal sharding mechanisms differ.
They can only be routed manually and have no automatic sharding.
None of them support scaling up capacity later.
why: 三者都按 key 分布数据，但内部单位不同：Cassandra 看 token/vnode，DynamoDB 看内部 partition，MongoDB 看 chunk。别把它们都说成同一套一致性哈希。
why_en: All three distribute data by key, but the internal unit differs: Cassandra uses tokens/vnodes, DynamoDB uses internal partitions, and MongoDB uses chunks. Do not describe them as one identical consistent-hashing implementation.
tradeoff: 假设三者机制'都一样'（省事但会答错扩容细节）vs 认真区分它们的路由/再平衡机制（面试官追问时更站得住脚）
codeSample:
# same idea: choose a key; different internal units

# Cassandra
partition_key = user_id
token = Murmur3(partition_key)
node = token_ring.owner(token)      # vnode/token range owns it

# DynamoDB
pk = user_id
internal_partition = aws_hash(pk)   # AWS may split/merge hot or large partitions

# MongoDB
shard_key = user_id                 # range or hashed shard key
chunk = find_chunk(shard_key)
shard = chunk.owner                 # balancer can migrate chunks
optionExplanations: 误解——三者里只有 Cassandra 真正接近经典 hash ring，DynamoDB 和 MongoDB 各有自己的分片单位，不能一概而论。
对，说清楚了共性和差异：都按 key 路由，但 Cassandra 用 token、DynamoDB 用 partition、MongoDB 用 chunk，各自迁移和再平衡方式不同。
误解——这三款都提供自动分片和路由，不需要工程师自己写路由层。
误解——它们都支持在线扩容，只是各自触发拆分/再平衡的方式不同。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — only Cassandra really resembles a classic hash ring; DynamoDB and MongoDB track distribution through their own internal units instead.
Right — the shared idea is key-based routing, but each engine tracks distribution differently: token ranges in Cassandra, hash partitions in DynamoDB, and migratable chunks in MongoDB.
Wrong — all three provide automatic partition routing, so you never hand-write a routing layer for any of them.
Wrong — all three support online scaling, they just differ in what triggers a split or rebalance.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 数据库，按 partition key 自动分布和扩展数据。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款文档型数据库，按 range 或 hash 分片键把数据切成 chunk，由后台 balancer 迁移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a document database that splits data into chunks by a range or hashed shard key, migrated by a background balancer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把节点和 key 映射到同一个 hash 环上，节点增减时只影响相邻的一小段范围。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps nodes and keys onto the same hash ring, so adding or removing a node only remaps a small neighboring range.

termDefinitions.meaning: Cassandra 用来把 key 映射到 token 环上的组件，例如 Murmur3Partitioner。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partitioner is the Cassandra component that maps keys onto the token ring, such as Murmur3Partitioner.

termDefinitions.meaning: Cassandra 里 token 是 hash 空间位置；vnode 是一台物理节点拥有的多个 token 范围，用来平衡数据和迁移压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In Cassandra, a token is a position in hash space; a vnode is one of many token ranges owned by a physical node to balance data and movement.

termDefinitions.meaning: MongoDB sharding 的迁移单位，是一段 range 或 hashed shard key 范围；balancer 会把 chunk 在 shard 间搬迁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A MongoDB chunk is the unit of migration: a range of the range or hashed shard key that the balancer can move between shards.

DynamoDB 不需要 partition key
所有用户固定写同一个 partition
以 user_id 为 partition key 自动路由
options_en: Store user_id in a log without ever creating a table.
DynamoDB doesn't need a partition key.
Write every user into the same fixed partition.
Use user_id as the partition key for automatic routing.

why_en: With DynamoDB, saying user_id is the partition key clearly states the distribution and access-pattern assumption.
whenOtherWins: 如果访问模式主要按 global secondary dimensions 查询，例如按时间全局扫事件，需要额外索引、流式聚合或不同存储模型。

Wrong — DynamoDB requires you to declare a partition key when you create the table; it isn't optional.
Wrong — cramming every user into one partition throws away distribution, so that single partition throttles all reads and writes.
Right — declaring user_id as the partition key lets DynamoDB route and scale automatically, matching how reads and writes actually target one user at a time.

q: 这个上限对你的容量规划意味着什么？
q_en: What does this ceiling mean for your capacity plan?
options: 既然还没到 256TiB，可以完全不用考虑分片，永远用单集群
单集群有天花板，按当前增速几个月内就逼近，需提前规划分片
只要升级到更贵的实例类型，存储上限就会消失
把索引全部删掉就能突破这个上限
options_en: Since we haven't hit 256TiB yet, we never need to consider sharding on a single cluster.
A single cluster has a ceiling; at this rate we approach it within months, so plan sharding now.
Upgrading to a pricier instance type makes the storage ceiling disappear.
Deleting all the indexes would break through this limit.
why: 单个数据库集群的存储不是无限的，Aurora 这类顶级云数据库也有量级上限（约 256TiB）。按当前翻倍速度推算多久会撞到天花板，才能判断该现在还是过几个月再开始做 sharding。
why_en: Even top-tier managed databases like Aurora have a storage ceiling, so projecting your growth rate against that ceiling tells you when sharding actually becomes necessary.
optionExplanations: 错——按每年翻倍的增速倒推，从 200TiB 涨到 256TiB 只要几个月，撞天花板并不遥远。
对，把当前 200TiB、翻倍速度和 256TiB 上限连起来看，几个月内就会顶到天花板，分片必须提前规划。
错——单集群存储上限是架构层面的物理约束，换更贵的实例规格改变不了它。
错——索引只影响表内查找速度，删掉它不会改变集群总存储容量的上限。

Right — chain 200TiB, a yearly doubling rate, and the ~256TiB cap together and you hit it within months, so sharding needs planning now.
Wrong — a single cluster's capacity is a structural limit of the architecture; switching to a pricier instance class doesn't lift it.
Wrong — indexes only affect lookup speed inside a table; deleting them does nothing to the cluster's overall storage cap.

options: 过早 sharding 不会改变系统复杂度
面试官一定希望所有系统一开始就分 100 个 shard
sharding 会自动让所有设计更简单
你引入了热点、跨 shard 查询、重平衡和一致性等复杂度，却没有证明这些成本必要

The interviewer definitely wants every system to start with 100 shards.
Sharding automatically makes every design simpler.

why: Sharding 是解决单库规模瓶颈的重武器，不是默认起点。先做 math，证明单库或复制不够，再引入它。
why_en: Premature sharding adds real operational and consistency complexity before proving the scale requires it.
optionExplanations: 错误，过早 sharding 确实会明显改变系统复杂度。
错误，好的面试官不会希望过早 sharding，而是看容量估算。
错误，sharding 反而增加复杂度。
正确，过早 sharding 会引入大量复杂度，但没有基于容量推导来证明必要。
optionExplanations_en: Incorrect; premature sharding significantly changes and increases system complexity.
Incorrect; good interviewers expect capacity math, not immediate sharding.
Incorrect; sharding adds complexity, not simplicity.
Correct; premature sharding introduces hotspots, cross-shard queries, and consistency complexity without justification.

q: 选择 shard key 错误通常会导致哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: What problems usually come from choosing the wrong shard key? (Select all that apply.)
options: 数据分布不均
热点 shard
常见查询不得不 fan-out 到所有 shard
所有数据库限制都会消失
options_en: Uneven data distribution
A hot shard
Common queries are forced to fan out to every shard
Every database limit simply disappears
why: fan-out 是查多个 shard 后 merge/aggregate；查询不带 shard key 时最容易发生。
why_en: A bad shard key causes imbalance, hot spots, and frequent fan-out queries: one query asks many shards and then merges or aggregates the results.
optionExplanations: 对，坏 key 会让某些取值扎堆，数据体积本身先失衡，这跟热点是两件事。
对，除了数据量不均，坏 key 还会让个别 shard 的请求量远高于其他节点，往往比容量问题更早触发告警。
对，常见查询不带 shard key 时，应用只能挨个问遍所有 shard 再合并结果，延迟和负载随 shard 数放大。
错，分片解决的是数据分布问题，不会让数据库本身的容量、一致性等限制凭空消失，这是常见误解。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a skewed key clusters values into a few buckets, so raw data volume goes lopsided before anything else shows up.
Right — beyond size, a bad key can push traffic onto one shard far more than the rest, often triggering alarms before storage does.
Right — queries that skip the shard key have to hit every shard and stitch results back together, so latency and load climb with shard count.
Wrong — sharding only redistributes data; it doesn't erase a database's own capacity or consistency limits, a common misconception.

q: 补全三种 sharding 策略的关键词：
q_en: Complete the keywords for the three sharding strategies.
text: {{Range}} sharding 简单且支持范围扫描；{{Hash}} sharding 默认更均匀；{{Directory}} sharding 最灵活但每次请求多一次 lookup。
why: Range 用原始 key 的商/区间，保留连续性；raw modulo 用余数把相邻 key 交错分桶；hash sharding 是先 H(key) 再取桶。三者别混。
why_en: Range sharding splits continuous ranges of the original key; hash sharding first scatters keys into hash space; directory sharding looks up an explicit mapping. They trade off range scans, balance, and flexibility.
codeSample:
# range / quotient: 连续 user_id 放一起
shard = user_id // 1_000_000      # 1..999999 -> shard 0

# raw modulo: 不 hash，只按余数交错分桶
bucket = user_id % 4              # 100->0, 101->1

# hash sharding: 先打散，再取桶/slot
slot = H(user_id) % 16384
shard = slot_owner[slot]

# directory: 查显式映射
shard = directory.get(user_id)

termDefinitions.meaning: 把原始 shard key 的连续值区间分配给不同 shard，例如 user_id 1–1M 到 shard 1。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Range-based sharding assigns continuous ranges of the shard key's values to different shards.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对 shard key 做 hash 后再取模，把结果映射到某个 shard。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash-based sharding hashes the shard key and maps the result to a shard, typically via modulo.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接用原始 key 的余数分桶，例如 user_id % 4；它会交错相邻 key，但不等于先 hash 打散。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A raw modulo bucket uses the original key's remainder, such as user_id % 4; it interleaves adjacent keys but is not the same as hashing first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用查找表或目录服务记录每个 key 当前在哪个 shard 上；目录服务可以由 DB、Redis、ZooKeeper、etcd 等承载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Directory-based sharding uses a lookup table or service that records which shard each key currently lives on.

termDefinitions.meaning: hash 函数输出的数字空间；hash sharding 切的是这个空间，而不是原始 key 的自然顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hash space is the numeric output space of a hash function; hash sharding splits this space, not the natural order of the original key.

tradeoff: 先算出目标 shard 再查询（一次请求，低延迟）vs 广播查询所有 shard（不用算，但延迟和负载高很多）

scenario: 你已经证明单库写吞吐撑不住，需要分片。面试官问你最重要的两个设计决策是什么。
scenario_en: You have proven that one database cannot handle the write throughput anymore, so sharding is needed. The interviewer asks for the two most important design decisions.
q: 你应该回答哪两个？
q_en: Which two design decisions should you answer with?
options: 选择是否用 dark mode，以及字体大小
选择 logo 颜色，以及 README 标题
选择前端框架，以及按钮圆角
选择 shard key，以及选择数据如何分布到 shards 的策略
options_en: Choosing dark mode, and the font size
Choosing the logo color, and the README title
Choosing the frontend framework, and the button corner radius
Choosing the shard key, and choosing the strategy for how data is distributed to shards
why: Shard key 决定“按什么字段分组”，distribution strategy 决定“这些 key 值怎么映射到机器”。同一个 user_id，可以 range、hash 或 directory 三种方式分布。
why_en: The shard key decides which field groups the data; the distribution strategy decides how those key values map to machines. The same user_id key can be distributed by range, hash, or directory.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统还没证明单库瓶颈，最重要的决策不是怎么 shard，而是先做容量估算和单库/复制方案评估。
tradeoff: shard key 选择（数据怎么分组）vs 分布策略选择（这些组怎么摊到机器上）——两个独立但相关的决策

Incorrect; logo and documentation are unrelated to sharding design.
Incorrect; frontend framework and button styles are unrelated to database sharding.
Correct; shard key choice and distribution strategy are the two core sharding design decisions.

scenario: 你想看真实代码层面如何同时做单机 partitioning 和应用层 sharding。
scenario_en: You want a concrete code-level example of single-database partitioning plus application-level sharding.
q: 这段代码里，partitioning 和 sharding 分别在哪里发生？
q_en: Where do partitioning and sharding happen in this code?
options: SQL 分区；Python 选 shard
SQL 索引；Python 做分区
partitioning 和 sharding 都只发生在 `ORDER BY created_at`
只要有多个表名，就一定已经跨多台机器 sharding
options_en: SQL partitions; Python picks the shard.
SQL indexes; Python partitions.
Both partitioning and sharding only happen in `ORDER BY created_at`.
Having multiple table names always means sharding across machines.
why: Partitioning 发生在单个 DB 内部，数据库根据 `created_at` 把行放进本地分区。Sharding 发生在应用/路由层，先根据 `user_id` 选择哪一个 DB 连接。
why_en: Partitioning happens inside one database: the database places rows into local partitions by created_at. Sharding happens in the application or routing layer: it chooses which database connection to use by user_id.
whenOtherWins: 生产系统常用 Vitess、Citus、MongoDB、Cassandra 或 DynamoDB 托管路由细节，但概念仍是先选分布 key，再决定数据落点。
tradeoff: 应用层手写 shard routing（直观但要自己处理扩容/迁移）vs 托管/中间件 sharding（省心但要理解其 key 选择限制）
optionExplanations: 正确，SQL 定义单机分区规则，Python 根据 user_id 选择数据库机器。
错误，index 是查询加速结构，不是跨机器分片；INSERT 只是写入动作。
错误，排序只决定返回顺序，不决定数据落在哪台机器或哪个分区。
错误，多表/多分区可以仍在同一台 DB；跨机器才是 sharding。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; SQL defines local partitioning, while Python chooses the database machine by user_id.
Incorrect; an index speeds queries but is not cross-machine sharding, and INSERT is just the write operation.
Incorrect; sorting controls result order, not which machine or partition stores the data.
Incorrect; multiple tables or partitions can still live on one database machine; sharding requires crossing machines.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一台持有部分数据的数据库实例；应用或中间件先选中它，再执行 SQL。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DB shard is a database instance that holds a subset of data; the app or middleware selects it before running SQL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个 DB 实例内部的表分区，例如按月份拆出的 orders_2026_06。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A local partition is a table partition inside one database instance, such as orders_2026_06.

scenario: 你要为不同系统选择 partition key，但同一个词在 SQL partitioning 和 NoSQL/DynamoDB 里含义层级不同。
scenario_en: You need to choose partition keys for different systems, but the term means different layers in SQL partitioning versus NoSQL or DynamoDB.
q: 哪些 partition key 选择通常合理？（多选）
q_en: Which partition-key choices are usually reasonable? (Select all that apply.)
options: 订单/交易表常按 created_at 做 SQL range partition，方便时间查询和历史清理
DynamoDB 用户资料表常用 user_id 做 partition key，方便 GetItem/Query 命中单用户
高写入事件表直接按 boolean is_premium 分区，通常能均匀打散负载
多租户 SaaS 常用 tenant_id 或 tenant 分配的 ID 段，让公司内查询局部化
options_en: Order or transaction tables often use created_at for SQL range partitioning to support time queries and retention.
A DynamoDB user profile table often uses user_id as the partition key so GetItem or Query targets one user.
A high-write event table should use boolean is_premium as the partition key to evenly spread load.
Multi-tenant SaaS often uses tenant_id or tenant-assigned ID ranges so per-company queries stay local.
why: 选 partition key 先看最常见查询和数据生命周期。SQL 里常用于 pruning/清理；DynamoDB 里更像分布 key。
why_en: Choose a partition key from the dominant query pattern and data lifecycle. In SQL, a partition key often enables pruning and retention; in DynamoDB-like NoSQL systems, it is closer to a distribution key that decides the internal partition.
codeSample:
-- SQL partitioning: partition key 帮 DB 跳过无关分区
PARTITION BY RANGE (created_at)  -- orders_2026_06, orders_2026_07

-- DynamoDB/NoSQL: partition key 更像分布 key
PK = user_id                    -- Get user profile by user_id

-- Chat: 常见组合
PK = chat_id                    -- 一个会话的消息放一起
SK = created_at                 -- 会话内按时间分页
whenOtherWins: 避免低基数字段如 boolean/status 单独做高写入 partition key；它们值太少，容易倾斜和热点。
tradeoff: 按查询模式选 key（读快、清理方便）vs 只追求均匀打散（可能破坏范围查询和局部性）
optionExplanations: 正确，时间范围 partition 适合订单、交易、日志这类按时间查和按时间清理的数据。
正确，DynamoDB 的 partition key 决定内部路由，user_id 适合用户资料的单用户访问。
错误，boolean 只有两个值，通常会造成严重倾斜，不能均匀打散高写入。
正确，多租户系统常按 tenant 边界访问，用 tenant_id 或 tenant ID 段能减少跨分区查询。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; time-range partitioning fits orders, transactions, and logs that are queried and retained by time.
Correct; DynamoDB's partition key drives internal routing, and user_id fits per-user profile access.
Incorrect; a boolean has only two values and usually creates severe skew rather than even distribution.
Correct; multi-tenant systems are often accessed by tenant boundary, so tenant_id or tenant ID ranges reduce cross-partition work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单个数据库内部用来选择表分区的字段，常用于 partition pruning 和历史数据清理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SQL partition key selects a table partition inside one database, often for partition pruning and retention.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 里决定 item 落到哪个内部分区的字段，更接近分布/路由 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DynamoDB partition key decides which internal partition an item lands in, closer to a distribution or routing key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把时间切成固定窗口，例如按小时、天或月分桶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time bucket groups timestamps into fixed windows such as hours, days, or months.

scenario: 一个系统可能既有跨机器 sharding，又有每台 DB 内部的 local partitioning。你要判断两层 key 是否应该相同。
scenario_en: A system may use both cross-machine sharding and local partitioning inside each DB. You need to decide whether the two keys should be the same.
q: 关于 shard key 和 partition key 是否选同一个，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about choosing the same or different shard and partition keys are correct? (Select all that apply.)
options: 用户资料表按 user_id 单点读写，NoSQL/DynamoDB 的 partition key 常可直接用 user_id
订单/聊天/日志常用一个 key 选机器，再用时间 key 做本地 partition
高写入系统应该把 created_at 同时作为 shard key 和 partition key
多租户 SaaS 若主要按公司访问，tenant_id 常适合作为 shard key
options_en: For user-profile point reads and writes, a NoSQL/DynamoDB partition key can often be user_id.
Orders, chat, and logs often use one key to choose the machine and a time key for local partitions.
High-write systems should use created_at as both the shard key and partition key.
For multi-tenant SaaS accessed mainly by company, tenant_id is often a good shard key.
why: 相同或不同都可以：同 key 适合用户/租户局部访问；不同 key 常用于一层选机器，一层按时间剪枝和清理。
why_en: Either can be right. The same key fits per-user or per-tenant locality; different keys are common when user_id/chat_id/tenant_id picks the machine and created_at or a time bucket handles local pruning and retention.
codeSample:
# same: NoSQL 用户资料
PK = user_id

# different: sharded SQL 订单
shard = hash(user_id) % N     # 选机器
part = month(created_at)      # 机内分区
idx = (user_id, -created_at)  # 分区内排序/查找
whenOtherWins: 如果同 key 会造成热点或难以清历史，就拆开：一个 key 管分布，另一个管时间剪枝。
tradeoff: 同 key（简单、局部性强）vs 不同 key（同时兼顾分布、时间查询和清理）
optionExplanations: 正确，用户资料通常按 user_id 访问，用 user_id 做分布/partition key 很自然。
正确，这类表常先按实体选机器，再按时间做本地分区和清理。
错误，created_at 单调递增，做 shard key 会把新写入压到最新范围形成热点。
正确，租户边界访问明显时，tenant_id 能让公司内数据局部化。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; user profiles are usually accessed by user_id, so user_id is a natural distribution or partition key.
Correct; these tables often choose the machine by entity and use time for local partitioning and retention.
Incorrect; created_at is monotonically increasing and can push new writes into the newest range hotspot.
Correct; when access follows tenant boundaries, tenant_id keeps company data local.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard key routes across machines and decides which DB shard receives the request or data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单个 DB shard 内部分区用的字段，常用于 pruning、排序范围和历史清理。

scenario: 订单表按 user_id sharding；现在要按 product_id 查全站订单。
scenario_en: Orders are sharded by user_id; now you need to query site-wide orders by product_id.
q: 这段代码体现了什么设计后果？
q_en: What design consequence does this code illustrate?
options: 非 shard key 查询可能 fan-out + merge
有 index 就不会跨 shard
跨 shard 写入不用协调
partition key 自动解决 join
options_en: A non-shard-key query may fan out and merge.
An index means cross-shard queries never happen.
Cross-shard writes need no coordination.
A partition key automatically fixes joins.
why: 按 user_id 单 shard；按 product_id 要 fan-out+merge；跨 shard 写要协调。
why_en: The shard key defines the fast path. A user_id query hits one shard; a product_id query finds data spread across user shards, so it fans out and merges. Cross-shard writes need saga or 2PC.
whenOtherWins: product_id 高频时，建 product_id 读模型，别每次 fan-out。
tradeoff: user_id sharding（用户快）vs product_id 读模型（产品快）vs fan-out（简单但贵）

错误，index 只加速 shard 内部。
错误，跨 shard 写需要协调。
错误，partition key 不会自动消除 join。
optionExplanations_en: Correct; by_product in the code visits every SHARD.
Incorrect; indexes are local to a shard.
Incorrect; cross-shard writes need coordination.
Incorrect; partition keys do not automatically remove joins.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out queries multiple shards and merges results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为某种查询额外维护的数据视图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A data view maintained for one query pattern.
